I teach courses in political science at the Department of Government, Law & Policy. My approach emphasizes the following: developing written and spoken presentation and argumentation skills with a heavy focus on critical thinking (partially through repeated question-answer sequences), real-world applications and implications of the subject material, hands-on data analysis with an eye on answering real-world inquiries.

## Teaching Interests

Introduction to Data Analysis · Data Visualization · Applied Data Analysis · Advanced Data Analysis · Comparative Politics · Political Behavior · Election Science · Local Elections and Local Politics · Authoritarianism & Populism · Media and Politics · Political Psychology · Comparing Democracies / Comparative Political Behavior · Public Opinion and Political Parties · Russian State & Politics · Politics of Developing Countries

## Fall 2026
I am teaching three courses in Fall 2026:

- **PLSC 30453** Introduction to Political Analysis (undergraduate)

- **PLSC 33203** Introduction to Comparative Politics (undergraduate)

- **PLSC 66003** Advanced Political Analysis (graduate) (co-teaching)
